A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLFFD research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained content across pagination and figure renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLFFD cross-dataset and cross-manipulation results, ablations, and qualitative visualizations, including additional experiments in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds MiniGPT-4 fine-tuning results and further attention-map comparisons.

M1.justification: Section 5 adds a supplementary MiniGPT-4 adaptation using PFIG-generated image-text pairs and fine-grained descriptions of original FF++ images to generate authenticity judgments and explanations. The original PFIG procedure, CLIP detector, C2F framework, and losses remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions cover FF++, DFD, DFDC-P, Celeb-DF, and Wild-Deepfake. The added MiniGPT-4 examples and heatmaps remain within existing domains and the existing goals of authenticity detection and artifact explanation; they introduce no additional dataset or population.

E2.justification: New Figure 6 compares PFIG-tuned MiniGPT-4 with untuned MiniGPT-4 and MiniGPT-4 tuned using coarse FF++ labels. Figure 9 adds UIA-ViT to the unseen-image attention comparison; v1 already compared it on FF++ examples. Comparator membership in Tables 1–7 is unchanged.

E3.justification: The new MiniGPT-4 experiment compares three tuning conditions using an authenticity question followed by a request for reasons. It introduces a separate fine-tuning and testing protocol. Existing quantitative detection protocols, metrics, and HQ/LQ settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds qualitative comparisons testing the effect of MiniGPT-4 fine-tuning supervision and further unseen-face attention cases against UIA-ViT. Existing component, backbone, supervision, and training-strategy ablations, including appendix analyses, are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates and qualitative examples without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additions introduce no statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical results, including Table 1 AUCs of 84.74 on DFDC-P and 84.80 on Celeb-DF. Figures 6 and 9 add qualitative findings. For example, one illustrated Celeb-DF forgery is called real by both MiniGPT-4 comparators but fake by the PFIG-tuned model.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 and Appendix A's four PFIG algorithms retain their mathematical content. The added MiniGPT-4 section introduces no formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract adds claims that multimodal-LLM integration enhances performance and demonstrates versatility. The introduction reframes novelty from introducing language supervision to introducing visual-language pretraining and multimodal learning. The central generalization and interpretability claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 5 interprets the new examples as evidence that PFIG supervision improves LLM judgments and explanations relative to coarse-label tuning. New appendix discussion attributes competing attention maps to microphone distraction and emphasizes subtle eye-color artifacts. Earlier interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Section 5 documents the MiniGPT-4 training-data construction, adaptation involving the image encoder, Q-former and projection layer, three training-question templates, evaluation questions, learning rate of 3e-5, and 224 × 224 inputs. Original implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to ImageNet and MiniGPT-4 and removes MesoNet and Jain et al.'s synthetic-alteration detection paper. Positioning expands toward LLM applicability and emphasizes visual-language pretraining; the existing related-work survey is largely retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and contribution list receive localized rewriting. A new LLM section and appendix discussion are added, and Haozhe Yang joins the author list. Most method and experimental prose and the overall organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the multi-model dialogue display in Figure 6 and unseen-image heatmaps in Figure 9. Earlier appendix Figures 6–7 become Figures 7–8. Existing diagrams and tables are retained, with accompanying text and table reflow.

improvement.justification: The MiniGPT-4 comparison and expanded unseen-image analysis add useful exploratory evidence for PFIG supervision and interpretability, with implementation information for the extension. The gain is limited: the LLM evidence consists of six illustrative examples and does not quantify the abstract's broader performance claim. The original quantitative evidence remains unchanged.
